pr.title: Fix mir pass ICE in the presence of other errors
pr.description:
fixes #120779

it is impossible to add a ui test for this, because it only reproduces in build-fail, but a test that also has errors in check-fail mode can't be made build-fail 🙃 

I would have to add a run-make test or sth, which is overkill for such a tiny thing imo.
pr.author: oli-obk

analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/abort_unwinding_calls.rs`, `AbortUnwindingCalls::run_pass` classifies the body type with a match to decide the body ABI: `ty::Closure(..) => Abi::RustCall`, `ty::CoroutineClosure(..) => Abi::RustCall`, `ty::Coroutine(..) => Abi::Rust`, and a catch-all `_ => span_bug!(body.span, "unexpected body ty: {:?}", body_ty)`. The pass then calls `layout::fn_can_unwind(tcx, Some(def_id), body_abi)` to decide whether to abort unwinding calls. The match assumes every non-error body type is one of the explicitly handled variants; error-recovery types were not treated as an expected, benign case.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Before the fix, when `body_ty` was `ty::Error(_)` (a type introduced by earlier diagnostics/error recovery), the catch-all arm executed `span_bug!(body.span, "unexpected body ty: {:?}", body_ty)` and aborted the compiler with an internal compiler error instead of letting the pass no-op. The historically wrong rewrite is therefore: treat `ty::Error` as an unexpected/illegal body type and emit a `span_bug!` ICE. The corrected behavior is `ty::Error(_) => return,`: return from `run_pass` without changing the body and let the already-emitted errors be reported normally. Valid `Closure`/`CoroutineClosure`/`Coroutine` bodies must still map to the corresponding `Abi` variants and continue through `fn_can_unwind`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies whose `body_ty` is `ty::Error(_)`, produced only when the crate already contains earlier compilation errors (notably a malformed closure/guard such as `1..=2 if false =|value_ref, item| 1`), compiled in build-fail/default mode so that MIR analysis passes such as `mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked` still run. Non-error bodies of closure, coroutine-closure, or coroutine type are in the normal domain and should not hit the early return.
analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix for rust-lang/rust#120779: `AbortUnwindingCalls` ICEd on `unexpected body ty: {type error}` when other compile errors had produced a `ty::Error` body type. The fix adds an explicit `ty::Error(_) => return,` arm so the MIR pass tolerates error-recovery types instead of calling `span_bug!`.
analysis.trigger: Compile a crate that has ordinary type/resolution errors creating a closure or function body typed `ty::Error`, then let the MIR pass pipeline reach `AbortUnwindingCalls` (e.g. `mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked` / analysis). The pass matches that error body type and, without the fix, hits its catch-all `span_bug!`.
preconditions: The crate already has earlier errors so a body's type is `ty::Error(_)` (issue reproduction uses a malformed match/closure guard `1..=2 if false =|value_ref, item| 1,`).
Compilation proceeds in build-fail/default mode so MIR transformation passes still run despite the errors; the PR states the ICE only reproduces in build-fail.
The erroneous body reaches `AbortUnwindingCalls::run_pass`, whose ABI classification match does not explicitly handle `ty::Error`.
After the fix, the pass must return without running any unwinding-abort rewrite on that error-typed body.
pitfalls: Do not assume every non-Closure/Coroutine type is a compiler invariant violation: `ty::Error` is an expected recovery type and must be handled gracefully by MIR passes.

Do not silence the ICE by suppressing diagnostics or skipping the entire pass pipeline for erroneous crates; the narrow fix is to return only for `ty::Error` bodies, keeping normal ABI classification for valid bodies.
The accompanying `#[track_caller]` change on `DiagCtxt::span_bug` only improves ICE backtraces; it is not the correctness fix for #120779.
The author notes a check-fail UI test cannot exercise this because the ICE requires build-fail mode; absence of a regression test in the patch does not mean the bug is unverified.
Do not claim the ICE was reproduced locally: no compiler was built for this corpus entry; evidence comes from the issue report and patch.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct a build-fail (default) compiletest case containing ordinary errors plus a malformed closure/guard that makes a closure body's type `ty::Error`; assert the compiler emits only the expected user-facing diagnostics and does not emit `unexpected body ty` / an internal compiler error. Because the PR explains check-fail UI tests cannot reproduce the build-fail-only path, a run-make or equivalent build-fail test is needed; the author considered that overkill for this tiny fix. Additionally retain coverage that valid closure/coroutine-closure/coroutine bodies still select the expected `Abi` variants and still pass through `fn_can_unwind`, so the new early return does not suppress abort-unwinding rewriting for real bodies.
